title: Making ecological programs work at scale | Science
description: Some of the rain that waters the crops of farmers in Argentina and Paraguay comes from moisture released by forests in Brazil. A forest’s contribution to people’s lives can extend well beyond the land it occupies—and the carbon it stores. Forests can moderate heat, reduce soil erosion, improve air and water quality, and provide habitat for wildlife. Investing in forests need not mean choosing nature over development. Well-designed ecological programs could potentially generate ecological and health benefits that justify their costs while remaining compatible with economic growth.
